description: The pie chart, titled "Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse," displays the distribution of media sources cited in a study, with each slice representing a different outlet and its corresponding percentage of total mentions. The chart is divided into 14 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media organization and a numerical value indicating its share. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to "Other" and accounts for 14% of the total. The second largest is "Drudge Report," shown in orange, with 8%. Several outlets are tied at 7%, including "The Daily Caller" (green) and "NPR" (purple). The "Huffington Post" (red) and "Vox" (brown) each represent 6%. "The Guardian" (pink) and "BBC" (light green) are both at 5%. The remaining outlets—RT (yellow), "Daily Kos" (light blue), "National Review" (cyan), "Daily Mail" (teal), "Red State" (dark green), "Fox News" (dark purple), "Shareblue" (light pink), and "PoliticusUSA" (magenta)—each contribute 3% to the total. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top right, with no visual emphasis such as exploded slices or special formatting. A legend is not present, but each segment is clearly labeled with both the media name and its percentage value directly on or near the slice.
